title: Buffers for Chloroplast Isolation from Diatoms
author: P. Dreux Chappell
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ea2bage

steps.title: Prepare Isolation Buffer
steps.instruction: Make 40 mL of isolation buffer by mixing 20 mL 1 M sorbitol, 400 µL 0.6 M Na₂‑EDTA, 200 µL 1 M MgCl₂, 400 µL 1 M KCl, 40 µL 1 M MnCl₂, 2 mL 1 M HEPES‑KOH (pH 8.0), and 16.96 mL sterile H₂O; add bovine serum albumin (BSA) to a final concentration of 1 % (w/v) immediately before use to the portion of buffer required at the start of the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Mix the listed reagents to a total volume of 40 mL.
Just before use, add BSA to achieve 1 % (w/v) in the aliquot needed.

steps.title: Prepare PEG‑6000 Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 6 g PEG‑6000 in 10 mL sterile water to obtain a 10 mL solution.

steps.title: Prepare Percoll Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Combine 19 mL Percoll with 1 mL PEG‑6000 solution, then add 0.2 g Ficoll and 0.2 g BSA; mix to a final volume of 20 mL.

steps.title: Prepare Gradient Mixture
steps.instruction: Mix 250 µL 1 M HEPES‑KOH (pH 8.0), 1 mL 0.1 M EDTA, 6.26 mL 1 M sorbitol, and 2.49 mL water to make a 10 mL stock solution.

steps.title: Prepare 3X Bottom Layer
steps.instruction: Mix 5.7 mL Percoll solution with 1.01 mL Gradient mixture to obtain the 80 % Percoll bottom layer.

steps.title: Prepare 3X Top Layer
steps.instruction: Mix 5.04 mL Percoll solution with 6.96 mL Gradient mixture to obtain the 40 % Percoll top layer.

steps.title: Prepare 10M Ammonium Fluoride
steps.instruction: Dissolve 3.7 g NH₄F in 10 mL H₂O to make a 10 M ammonium fluoride solution.
